title: A second phone on an older app version quietly wipes newer workout details from the saved copy
what: A member signed in on two phones, one updated and one not, logs a treadmill set with speed, incline or level on the new phone. The older phone brings that workout in, but it cannot keep those details. On its next save it sees its own version as changed, even though nobody touched it, and sends it to the server as the newest edit. The server copy, and then the new phone, lose the speed, incline and level. The app never refuses a record from a newer version here, because new details were added without raising the format number. A backup file from the newer app restored on an older app also drops those details with no word.
expected: An older phone never overwrites the saved copy with less than it received: it either keeps what it cannot read, or stops and asks the member to update. A record from a newer format is refused with the update message, as backup files already are.
who: members signed in on two phones running different app versions
how_often: every time a new detail is added to workouts and one phone is not updated
fix_line: After bringing a record in, remember the phone's own version of it, and refuse records newer than this app understands.

title: A member under 18 who was already saving keeps everything on MettleUp's server after the under-18 fix
what: The new under-18 rule only stops new saving. A member aged 10 to 17 who signed in before the fix already has their age, body weight and workouts on MettleUp's server. After the update nothing removes that copy; the only thing that ever deletes it is the member pressing Delete my account. The privacy notice says such data is deleted once MettleUp learns the member is under 18, and the phone does learn it.
expected: When the phone sees an under-18 profile on a signed-in account, the copy already on the server is deleted once, and the member is told their workouts now stay on this phone only.
who: members under 18 who signed in before the fix
fix_line: When the age rule stops saving, also delete the server copy once and say so on the backup line.

items.reason: Fresh install: bring-back after sign-in (existing ids). Update: backup files and Drive backups of every older version, including the old ForgeAI app, are still read; the local copy tables are made once by version; empty trailing fields are trimmed so old records keep their fingerprint; the sign-in survives the address switch. Two phones on different versions: new finding 01. Sideload vs Play: one package id for both; Google sign-in needs each build's signing key registered (FN-L14-03). Watch and panel cache: nothing of the kind in this area.

Trial or plan end: Plus limits are switched off and only block adding more, never remove data. Gym pauses, closes, member leaves: the saved copy is not tied to a gym (offered to everyone). Staff leaves: deleting keeps an owner or trainer sign-in. Owner changes phone: bring-back (existing ids). Year end and leap day: dates use the phone's own calendar, no month arithmetic; Drive keep-one-a-day uses world time (FN-L16-03). Not opened for 6 months: the server copy has no expiry and waiting changes are retried on the next open (FN-B-run-a-02); the live server's sign-in expiry setting was not read (no dashboard), the local config sets none.

New flows checked for old users: Drive backup stopping (old Drive phones get a one-time card), the account for everyone (nudge after 3 workouts), phone number sign-in (also in Settings, not only the welcome), server address switch (old sign-in still read), under-18 rule (stops new saving only: finding 02).
Paths exist for every case except under-18 members already saving: their server copy has no clean-up short of deleting the account.

The only update mark tied to this area is the Backups moved card. It needs a Drive link from an older version, so a fresh install never sees it; a new member who links Drive only to restore an old backup does see it, which is still true for them. No dots or What's new marks live in these folders.
Rule applied: no new mark shown on something not new to the member.
